Remember one point: maintenance workers are the general practitioners of buildings. They handle everyday ailments, refer difficult problems to specialists, and oversee routine health.
It does not suit people who only want office work, dislike climbing or crouching, or avoid dirty tasks. Maintenance workers are versatile generalists, and dirty, tiring work is routine.

A common path is electrical, plumbing, or other skills training or technical school, relevant credentials such as an electrician certificate, entry through property maintenance, accumulated experience in plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and masonry, then advancement toward property supervisor, engineering supervisor, or specialized refrigeration or low-voltage repair.

This work suits hands-on people who know a little about many trades and are willing to move around work sites. If you can resolve leaks, tripped circuits, and broken locks in one visit, the field fits you.

Maintenance and Repair Workers, General maintain and make minor repairs to building plumbing, electrical, lighting, pipes, doors, windows, locks, and small equipment. They perform preventive maintenance and respond to breakdowns to keep facilities operating normally.

paragraphs: Three repair tickets arrive first thing in the morning. A top-floor resident reports low water pressure, so you inspect the water meter and look for leaks. Next, a corridor light flickers, requiring a ballast replacement. In the afternoon, a shopping center reports an air conditioner that does not cool; you inspect the filter and compressor, provide an emergency response, and contact a specialist. In the evening, enter the work orders into the system and replenish used spare parts.

In short, they repair whatever breaks across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, masonry, and HVAC systems. Work includes facility inspections, fault diagnosis, minor repairs, preventive maintenance, and work-order records.

AI can infer seven out of ten faults from a repair request, but when the top-floor resident reports fluctuating water pressure, you still have to inspect floor by floor and test repeatedly to determine whether the cause is the meter, a valve, or a leak inside the wall.

U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show about 1,629,700 maintenance and repair workers employed in 2024, projected to rise to 1,692,100 by 2034. That is a net increase of about 62,400 jobs, with roughly 159,800 annual openings. Median annual pay is about $48,600 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace general maintenance and repair workers, but it will take over work-order routing, spare-parts management, and recordkeeping. On-site diagnosis and hands-on repair remain genuine trades that machines cannot replace in the short term.

paragraphs: A 4/10 score means repair requests, spare parts, and records form a substantial part of the job and systems are taking them over. On-site diagnosis and hands-on repair remain the human domain, leaving limited room for AI replacement.

Medium-to-high exposure does not mean the work stays unchanged. AI routes tickets, manages parts, and suggests diagnoses, but hands still complete the repair. Pressure falls on helpers who only replace light bulbs or clean. Buildings still depend on versatile maintenance workers who understand plumbing and electricity, service refrigeration, and solve difficult faults.

To enter the field, study electrical work or plumbing at a technical school and earn an electrician credential. In the AI era, do not learn only component replacement; build plumbing, electrical, refrigeration, and low-voltage skills. Broader ability creates stability, and all-round maintenance workers remain scarce.

Let systems handle repair tickets and spare parts while you develop integrated maintenance and energy-efficiency retrofit skills. Earn refrigeration and low-voltage credentials and advance toward engineering supervision or specialized repair instead of stopping at light-bulb replacement.

Before changing careers into maintenance, earn credentials and begin in property maintenance. On a résumé, results such as independently resolving XX types of faults or maintaining XX buildings are more useful than a list of skills.

Test safety procedures before craftsmanship when hiring maintenance workers; reject anyone careless about energized work. Prioritize credentialed people with multiple skills, and offer credential subsidies to improve retention.

This field suits people who keep tools close and notice work that needs doing. When the repair queue reaches zero, you know your hands prevented several problems in the building that day.

The greatest satisfaction comes from solving difficult faults. After three days without finding a leak, you locate the pipe inside a wall by listening and reading water traces. The moment the repair succeeds is deeply rewarding.
If you accept sweating, constant movement, and frequent dirty work while taking every small repair seriously, this is a stable field. Maintenance workers earn their living by being dependable.

subject.summary: General maintenance workers keep buildings operating normally. Pipes, circuits, locks, and air conditioners all fall within their reach when they break, and residents' ability to live normally measures performance.
